proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established a sharp local Fisher bias radius, a lawful covariate-only two-coordinate LAN subexperiment, and a pointwise minimax lower bound G + v r(κ). A reviewer rejected the stronger outcome-tilted path and full restricted-EIF lower-bound claim; the repaired package remained incremental because it has no executable certified AKS correction, positive-gap upper-risk theorem, or coverage result. The zero-gap fallback lemma still has an undeclared product-rate use, so this archive is terminal below the field floor with an unrepaired proof gap, not a fully discharged theorem package.
tldr: Repeated-cross-section DiD has a published robustness--efficiency tradeoff: Sant'Anna--Xu provide the robust and stationarity-restricted influence-function geometry and suggest adaptation, while Armstrong--Kline--Sun solve an abstract Gaussian decision problem. The contribution here is narrower and fully causal. A covariate-only full-law tilt, which leaves the entire potential-outcome kernel fixed, attains the exact Fisher-radius composition bias and yields a two-coordinate Gaussian lower subexperiment with stationary variance \(G=E[g^2]\), not the full restricted EIF variance. This gives the pointwise lower bound \(G+v r(\kappa)\), not an adaptive upper-risk theorem. Paired cross-fitting is globally orthogonal under the actual learner rates, and the exact-zero threshold falls back to the robust estimator. At shrinking positive gaps, same-\(v_n\) lawful arrays can be Gaussian or compound Poisson, so \(v_n\) alone cannot define a frontier. The displayed AKS correction and bounded-bias interval are schematic oracle-Gaussian objects until executable numerical and covariance plug-in certification is supplied.
gap: The published DiD paper supplies the two influence functions, bias identity, efficiency gap, and a suggestion to adapt, while the published adaptation paper begins from an abstract Gaussian bias coordinate. Neither establishes which Gaussian biases and information coordinates are realized by lawful composition changes in a causal DiD model.
fill: The project constructs the lawful least-favorable family, proves the sharp Fisher-radius equality and two-coordinate LAN experiment on the finite-support interior class, and transfers the resulting local-minimax lower bound, but no estimator upper bound, to the published supermodel. Fold-specific orthogonal implementation and the exact-zero boundary are retained only as supporting lemmas.
